s0003.literal: Xie Zhe; Xiao Gan; Xie Geng; Zhang Zhong; Wang Gu; Kong Huan; Xiao Yun, with his younger brother Yin cited
s0003.idiomatic: Xie Zhe; Xiao Gan; Xie Geng; Zhang Zhong; Wang Gu; Kong Huan; Xiao Yun, with his younger brother Yin cited

s0004.literal: Xie Zhe, styled Yingyu, was a native of Yangxia in Chen commandery.
s0004.idiomatic: Xie Zhe, styled Yingyu, came from Yangxia in Chen commandery.

s0005.literal: His grandfather Tian was Minister of Works of Liang.
s0005.idiomatic: His grandfather Tian had been Liang's minister of works.

s0006.literal: His father Yue was Right Grandee with the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon of Liang.
s0006.idiomatic: His father Yue was a right grandee with the gold seal and purple ribbon under Liang.

s0007.literal: Zhe was handsome in bearing, refined and easy in deportment, yet open and clear in temperament; gentlemen esteemed him.
s0007.idiomatic: Zhe was handsome and graceful in manner, with a temperament open and clear; men of worth held him in esteem.

s0008.literal: He began his career as Secretariat Gentleman of Liang and rose through successive posts to Administrator of Guangling.
s0008.idiomatic: He entered service as a secretariat gentleman of Liang and rose step by step to administrator of Guangling.

s0009.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion, because his mother was aged he lodged at Guangling; when the Founder crossed the river from Jingkou to link up with Guo Yuanjian, Zhe then pledged his allegiance and was deeply respected.
s0009.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion his mother was old, so he stayed at Guangling. When the Founder crossed from Jingkou to join Guo Yuanjian, Zhe pledged himself to him and won deep regard.

s0010.literal: When the Founder was Governor of [Southern] Xuzhou, Editorial footnote marker 1. he memorialized Zhe as chief clerk.
s0010.idiomatic: When the Founder was governor of Southern Xuzhou,[1] he memorialized Zhe as chief clerk.

s0011.literal: When Jingzhou fell, the Founder sent Zhe to present a memorial to the Prince of Jin'an urging accession.
s0011.idiomatic: After Jingzhou fell, the Founder sent Zhe to the Prince of Jin'an with a memorial urging him to take the throne.

s0012.literal: Emperor Jing, acting on the regency, summoned him as Supervising Attendant in the Yellow Gate and concurrently Colonel of Foot Soldiers.
s0012.idiomatic: Emperor Jing, exercising the regency, summoned him as supervising attendant in the Yellow Gate and made him colonel of foot soldiers as well.

s0013.literal: When the Marquis of Zhenyang usurped the throne, he made Zhe Regular Attendant of the Direct and Upright Scattered Cavalry and attendant to the Eastern Palace.
s0013.idiomatic: When the Marquis of Zhenyang seized the throne, he named Zhe regular attendant of the direct and upright scattered cavalry and attendant to the eastern palace.

s0014.literal: When Emperor Jing took the throne, he was promoted to chief clerk concurrent with palace attendant.
s0014.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing succeeded, Zhe was promoted to chief clerk with concurrent appointment as palace attendant.

s0015.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate, Zhe was transferred to Minister of the Masters of Writing for Revenue, metropolitan governor of Yuzhou, and Minister of the Masters of Writing for Officials.
s0015.idiomatic: When the Founder took the Mandate, Zhe became minister of the masters of writing for revenue, metropolitan governor of Yuzhou, and minister of the masters of writing for officials.

s0016.literal: He went out as Clear Martial General and Administrator of Jinling; he entered court as Director of the Secretariat.
s0016.idiomatic: He went out as clear martial general and administrator of Jinling, then returned to court as director of the secretariat.

s0017.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded, he was made Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
s0017.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded, he was made mentor to the heir apparent.

s0018.literal: He went out as Clear Martial General and Interior Administrator of Hengyang, with salary of middle two thousand dan.
s0018.idiomatic: He was posted as clear martial general and interior administrator of Hengyang, with salary of middle two thousand dan.

s0019.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Changsha; his generalship and augmented salary remained as before.
s0019.idiomatic: He was moved to administrator of Changsha, keeping his general's title and augmented salary unchanged.

s0020.literal: On returning he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Director of the Secretariat.
s0020.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and director of the secretariat.

s0021.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, he held his former posts and additionally led the Vanguard General.
s0021.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, Zhe kept his offices and was also made to lead the vanguard general.

s0022.literal: When Emperor Xuan was overseer of the masters of writing, he drew Zhe in as palace attendant, Humane Martial General, and chief clerk on the left of the Minister of Works.
s0022.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan oversaw the masters of writing, he brought Zhe in as palace attendant, humane martial general, and left chief clerk to the minister of works.

s0023.literal: Before he could take up the appointment, he died in the first year of Guangda, aged fifty-nine.
s0023.idiomatic: He died in Guangda year 1 (567) before he could assume the post, at the age of fifty-nine.

s0024.literal: Posthumously he was given palace attendant and Director of the Secretariat in oversight, with posthumous title Kangzi.
s0024.idiomatic: He was posthumously made palace attendant and overseer of the secretariat, with the posthumous title Kangzi.

s0025.literal: Xiao Gan, styled Siti, was a native of Lanling.
s0025.idiomatic: Xiao Gan, styled Siti, came from Lanling.

s0026.literal: His grandfather Yi was Chancellor of Qi and Prince Wenxian of Yuzhang.
s0026.idiomatic: His grandfather Yi was chancellor of Qi and Prince Wenxian of Yuzhang.

s0027.literal: His father Zifan was Director of the Secretariat of Liang.
s0027.idiomatic: His father Zifan was director of the secretariat under Liang.

s0028.literal: Gan's bearing was elegant and correct, his nature quiet and spare; he excelled at clerical script and obtained the method of his uncle's son Ziyun.
s0028.idiomatic: Gan was elegant and correct in deportment, quiet and spare by nature. He excelled at clerical script and mastered the hand of his cousin Ziyun.

s0029.literal: At nine sui he was summoned to fill a vacancy as National University student in the Zhou Changes; Yuan Ang of Liang, then Director of the National University as Minister of Works, deeply respected him.
s0029.idiomatic: At nine he was called to fill a vacancy as a National University student in the Zhou Changes. Yuan Ang of Liang, then director of the university in his capacity as minister of works, held him in deep regard.

s0030.literal: At fifteen he passed the classics licentiate examination.
s0030.idiomatic: At fifteen he passed the classics licentiate examination.

s0031.literal: He doffed the commoner's garb as aide in the law office on the staff of the Eastern Headquarters of the Prince of Xiangdong, and was promoted to Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household.
s0031.idiomatic: He left common status as law-office aide on the Prince of Xiangdong's eastern headquarters staff, then rose to attendant in the heir apparent's household.

s0032.literal: When the Marquis of Jian'an, Xiao Zhengli, went out to garrison South Yuzhou, Gan was again commissioned as recording secretary.
s0032.idiomatic: When the Marquis of Jian'an, Xiao Zhengli, took up his post in South Yuzhou, Gan was again commissioned recording secretary.

s0033.literal: He rose through successive posts to central recording secretary and advisory aide on the staff of the Prince of Xuancheng in the Central Army.
s0033.idiomatic: He rose step by step to central recording secretary and advisory aide on the Prince of Xuancheng's staff in the central army.

s0034.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, the Founder garrisoned South Xuzhou and drew Gan in as Trustworthy Martial General and attendant gentleman on the Minister of Works staff.
s0034.idiomatic: After Hou Jing fell, the Founder held South Xuzhou and brought Gan in as trustworthy martial general and attendant gentleman on the minister of works staff.

s0035.literal: He was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman and Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.
s0035.idiomatic: He was promoted to secretariat gentleman and director of the heir apparent's household.

s0036.literal: Xie Geng, styled Hanmao, was a native of Yangxia in Chen commandery.
s0036.idiomatic: Xie Geng, styled Hanmao, came from Yangxia in Chen commandery.

s0037.literal: His grandfather Yao was Grandee with the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon of Qi.
s0037.idiomatic: His grandfather Yao was a grandee with the gold seal and purple ribbon under Qi.

s0038.literal: His father Ju was Central Guard General and General with the Staff Equal in Ceremony to the Three Excellencies of Liang.
s0038.idiomatic: His father Ju was central guard general and a general with staff equal in ceremony to the three excellencies under Liang.

s0039.literal: His two sons were Yan and
s0039.idiomatic: He had two sons, Yan and

s0042.literal: Editorial footnote marker 3. Yan reached the posts of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, palace attendant, censor-in-chief, and Minister of Ceremonies, and went out as overseer of East Yangzhou.
s0042.idiomatic: [3] Yan rose to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, palace attendant, censor-in-chief, and minister of ceremonies, and went out as overseer of East Yangzhou.

s0043.literal: In the second year of Zhenming he died at Kuaiji and was posthumously given Central Guardian General.
s0043.idiomatic: He died at Kuaiji in Zhenming year 2 (583) and was posthumously made central guardian general.

s0044.literal: Zhang Zhong, styled Shimiao, was a native of Wu commandery.
s0044.idiomatic: Zhang Zhong, styled Shimiao, came from Wu commandery.

s0045.literal: His grandfather Bian was Right Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works of Song and Administrator of Guangzhou.
s0045.idiomatic: His grandfather Bian was right chief clerk to Song's minister of works and administrator of Guangzhou.

s0046.literal: His father Lue was Junior Mentor in the Heir Apparent's Household of Liang and Administrator of Linhai.
s0046.idiomatic: His father Lue was junior mentor in the heir apparent's household under Liang and administrator of Linhai.

s0047.literal: Zhong from youth was quiet and still, correct in dwelling and deportment, and did not make friends lightly; none pressed in upon him, and people of the time said of him: "Song praised Fu and Yan; Liang had Juan and Chong.
s0047.idiomatic: From youth Zhong was quiet and still, correct in his home and bearing, and would not court company idly. No one forced his door. People said, "Song praised Fu and Yan; under Liang it was Juan and Chong.

s0048.literal: In the pure and lofty scholarly ideal, Zhong has that air.
s0048.idiomatic: In the love of purity and emptiness, Zhong carries that spirit.

s0049.literal: " He served in the law office of a Liang princely establishment, was promoted to external military aide, and left office on his father's death.
s0049.idiomatic: " He served in a Liang prince's law office, rose to external military aide, and resigned when his father died.

s0050.literal: When mourning ended, he became chief secretary on the staff of the Prince of Xuancheng in the Central Army.
s0050.idiomatic: After mourning he became chief secretary on the Prince of Xuancheng's staff in the central army.

s0051.literal: Zhong was then over forty; his household was poor, and he sought the magistracy of Shifeng; he entered court and was appointed western bureau aide on the staff of the Marquis of Xichang in the Central Guard.
s0051.idiomatic: Zhong was then past forty and poor at home, so he sought the magistracy of Shifeng. He entered court as western bureau aide on the Marquis of Xichang's staff in the central guard.

s0052.literal: At the time the Prince of Wuling was Inspector of Yizhou and chose his staff with care; he made Zhong eastern bureau aide on the campaign-west staff, but Zhong declined on the ground that his mother was aged, submitted a memorial in protest, was impeached by the relevant offices, and was dismissed from office.
s0052.idiomatic: The Prince of Wuling was then inspector of Yizhou and chose his staff carefully. He named Zhong eastern bureau aide on the campaign-west staff, but Zhong pleaded an aged mother, protested in a memorial, was impeached, and was removed from office.

s0053.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Zhong escorted his mother east in flight; after a long time he reached his native district.
s0053.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion Zhong fled east with his mother and only after long hardship reached home.

s0054.literal: Soon his mother died. Zhong was then fifty, yet his grief had wasted him beyond measure; moreover famine pressed him, and he could not bury her in season. Though the mourning term was complete, in dwelling and in food and drink he was always as if still in mourning.
s0054.idiomatic: His mother soon died. Zhong was fifty, wasted beyond measure by grief, and famine kept him from a timely burial. When the mourning term ended, he still ate and lived as though the coffin had not left the house.

s0055.literal: When Jing was pacified, Minister of Works Wang Sengbian reported the situation
s0055.idiomatic: After Jing fell, Minister of Works Wang Sengbian reported the facts

s0057.literal: Adopted reading: memorialized to the throne, Editorial footnote marker 4. and appointed him Trustworthy Martial General and Directing Secretary; he also provided the full funeral rites, and only when the burial was finished did Zhong put off mourning garb.
s0057.idiomatic: and memorialized to the throne.[4] Zhong was raised to trustworthy martial general and directing secretary. Sengbian also furnished the full funeral. Only when the burial was done did Zhong lay mourning aside.

s0058.literal: Sengbian also, because Zhong was aged and had no heir at his side, bestowed a concubine on him together with household furnishings.
s0058.idiomatic: Because Zhong was old and childless, Sengbian also gave him a concubine and furnishings for his home.

s0059.literal: Zhong was deep, still, and empty within, yet his discernment and capacity were vast; men of the time all regarded him as material for a chief minister.
s0059.idiomatic: Zhong was deep, still, and inwardly empty, yet his judgment and reach were broad. All who knew him took him for a future chief minister.

s0060.literal: Vice Director Xu Ling once submitted a memorial yielding his place to Zhong, saying: "Your servant Zhong's talent is deep and close-woven, his letters and histories abundant; a noble shoot of the southeast, a kinsman in talent whom the court cherishes—he can strengthen its plans and rightly should hold the left hand.
s0060.idiomatic: Vice Director Xu Ling once memorialized to yield his seat to Zhong: "Zhong's gifts are deep and close-held, his command of letters and histories ample. He is a fine scion of the southeast and a man the court should cherish. He can fortify the state's designs and rightly should hold the left hand.

s0061.literal: " Such was the weight in which his age held him.
s0061.idiomatic: " Such was the esteem in which his age held him.

s0062.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian he died, aged seventy; posthumously he was given Special Advancement, with posthumous title Yuanzi.
s0062.idiomatic: He died in Taijian year 5 (573), aged seventy, and was posthumously made special advancement with the title Yuanzi.

s0063.literal: Zhong was humane, forgiving, and of few desires; though he long held eminent posts, his household goods were repeatedly empty, yet all day he was at ease and did not count it a hardship.
s0063.idiomatic: Zhong was humane, forgiving, and wanting little. Though he long held high office, his house was often bare, yet he remained easy all day and did not call it hardship.

s0064.literal: Early in Taijian his daughter became consort to the Prince of Shixing; because her dwelling was mean and remote, she was specially granted one residence, and repeatedly granted the stipend of a county marquis of Wuxi and Jiaxing.
s0064.idiomatic: Early in Taijian his daughter married the Prince of Shixing. Because her quarters were poor and remote, the court granted her a house and repeatedly gave her a county marquis's stipend from Wuxi and Jiaxing.

s0065.literal: Editorial footnote marker 5. Once at Wuxi he saw a heavily fettered prisoner in jail; the weather was cold, and he called him out to sun himself, whereupon the man escaped. Emperor Wen laughed greatly and did not punish him severely.
s0065.idiomatic: [5] Once at Wuxi he saw a heavily shackled prisoner in jail. The day was cold, and he had the man brought out to warm in the sun; the prisoner escaped. Emperor Wen laughed and did not punish him harshly.

s0066.literal: He left a collected works in fourteen juan.
s0066.idiomatic: He left collected works in fourteen juan.

s0067.literal: Zhong's younger brother Ling was likewise quiet and possessed discernment; he reached chief clerk on the left of the Minister of Works, died in the eleventh year of Taijian aged seventy, and was posthumously given Grandee with the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
s0067.idiomatic: Zhong's younger brother Ling was likewise still and discerning. He rose to left chief clerk to the minister of works, died in Taijian year 11 (579) at seventy, and was posthumously made grandee with the gold seal and purple ribbon.

s0068.literal: Zhong's clansman Zhi Cai; of Qi Protector-General
s0068.idiomatic: Zhong's clansman Zhi Cai was grandson of

s0071.literal: Editorial footnote marker 6. From youth he was orphaned, independent, and upright; he served as Director of the Gold Bureau in the Masters of Writing.
s0071.idiomatic: [6] Orphaned early, he stood alone and upright. He served as director of the gold bureau in the masters of writing.

s0072.literal: He was promoted to Right Assistant Director, Magistrate of Jiankang, Commissioner of the Grand Fleet, Editorial footnote marker 7. and Directing Attendant of Yangzhou, concurrently Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
s0072.idiomatic: He rose to right assistant director, magistrate of Jiankang, commissioner of the grand fleet,[7] directing attendant of Yangzhou, and concurrent regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

s0073.literal: Sent on mission to Zhou, on return he was made Minister of Agriculture and Minister of Justice.
s0073.idiomatic: Sent on embassy to Zhou, he returned to be minister of agriculture and minister of justice.

s0074.literal: In every post he was known for purity and integrity.
s0074.idiomatic: Every office he held won him a name for clean conduct.

s0075.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, he was appointed palace attendant and Grandee with the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
s0075.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, he was made palace attendant and grandee with the gold seal and purple ribbon.

s0076.literal: At the time Emperor Xuan was assisting in government; because Gu was a maternal kinsman of the Deposed Emperor, wet nurses constantly came and went within the forbidden quarters and often conveyed secret orders. When the affair leaked out they were on the verge of execution, Editorial footnote marker 8. but Emperor Xuan, considering that Gu by nature had no military power and his dwelling and conduct were pure, only removed him from his posts and placed him under house arrest.
s0076.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan was then regent. Gu, as the Deposed Emperor's kin by marriage, had wet nurses passing in and out of the inner palace who often carried secret orders. When the plot came out they were nearly executed,[8] but Emperor Xuan judged that Gu had no troops at his back and lived cleanly, so he only stripped his offices and confined him.

s0077.literal: In the second year of Taijian, following precedent, he was made Inviting-from-Afar General and advisory aide on the staff of the Prince of Yuzhang, Xuanhui.
s0077.idiomatic: In Taijian year 2 (574), by the usual rule, he was made inviting-from-afar general and advisory aide to the Prince of Yuzhang, Xuanhui.

s0078.literal: He was promoted to Grand Master of the Palace, Minister of Ceremonies, and metropolitan governor of South Xuzhou.
s0078.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand master of the palace, minister of ceremonies, and metropolitan governor of South Xuzhou.

s0079.literal: In the seventh year he died in office, aged sixty-three.
s0079.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died in office, aged sixty-three.

s0080.literal: Posthumously he was given Grandee with the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
s0080.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grandee with the gold seal and purple ribbon.

s0081.literal: Whatever the funeral required was supplied as the occasion arose.
s0081.idiomatic: Whatever the funeral required was furnished as need arose.

s0082.literal: In the second year of Zhide his burial was changed, with posthumous title Gongzi.
s0082.idiomatic: In Zhide year 2 (584) he was reburied and given the posthumous title Gongzi.

s0083.literal: Gu was pure, empty, and of few desires, and was famed for filial piety in mourning.
s0083.idiomatic: Gu was pure, spare, and wanting little, and won fame for filial mourning.

s0084.literal: He also devoutly believed in the Buddhist law; when he completed mourning for his birth mother he thereafter ate only vegetables, sat in meditation by night, recited Buddhist sutras by day, and also studied the Chengshi treatises, yet he was not skilled in Dark Learning discourse.
s0084.idiomatic: He also devoutly followed the Buddhist teaching. After mourning for his birth mother he ate only vegetables for life, meditated by night, recited sutras by day, and studied the Chengshi commentarial tradition, but excelled little in Dark Learning talk.

s0085.literal: Once on embassy to Western Wei, at a feast he asked that the killing of a sheep be stopped; the sheep knelt and bowed before Gu.
s0085.idiomatic: On embassy to Western Wei, at a banquet he asked that a sheep slated for slaughter be spared; the sheep knelt and bowed before him.

s0086.literal: Again at a feast at Kunming Pool the Wei people, knowing southerners love fish, set out nets on a great scale; Gu invoked the Buddhist spell over them, and not a single scale was taken.
s0086.idiomatic: At another feast on Kunming Pool the Wei hosts, knowing southerners relish fish, spread great nets. Gu chanted Buddhist spells, and not one fish was caught.

s0087.literal: His son Kuan reached chief clerk on the left of the Minister of Works and palace attendant.
s0087.idiomatic: His son Kuan rose to left chief clerk to the minister of works and palace attendant.

s0088.literal: Kong Huan, styled Xiuwen, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
s0088.idiomatic: Kong Huan, styled Xiuwen, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji.

s0089.literal: His great-grandfather Xiuzhi was Left Minister of the People of Qi and Administrator of Wuxing.
s0089.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xiuzhi was left minister of the people under Qi and administrator of Wuxing.

s0090.literal: His grandfather Tai was Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household and Gentleman in the Three Excellencies Bureau of the Masters of Writing.
s0090.idiomatic: His grandfather Tai was attendant in the heir apparent's household and gentleman in the three excellencies bureau of the masters of writing.

s0091.literal: His father Zhisun was Registrar to the Princess of Zhijiang, Branch of Ningyuan, of Liang, and Magistrate of Wuxi.
s0091.idiomatic: His father Zhisun was registrar to the Princess of Zhijiang, branch of Ningyuan, under Liang, and magistrate of Wuxi.

s0092.literal: Huan was orphaned at several sui and was reared by his uncle Qiansun.
s0092.idiomatic: Huan lost his father when he was only a few years old and was raised by his uncle Qiansun.

s0093.literal: He loved learning and was skilled at composition; the classics, histories, and the hundred schools—none did he fail to traverse.
s0093.idiomatic: He loved learning and wrote well. Classics, histories, and the hundred schools alike lay open to him.

s0094.literal: Liu Xian of Pei, then called a storehouse of learning, whenever discussed with Huan would deeply admire him; he took Huan's hand and said: "In old days Cai Yong's tomb texts all went to Wang Can; I shall hope to match that Lord Cai—you need not fall short of the Wang clan."
s0094.idiomatic: Liu Xian of Pei, then hailed as a treasury of learning, debated with Huan and came away deeply impressed. He took Huan's hand and said, "Once Cai Yong's tomb classics all passed to Wang Can. I would match that Lord Cai; you need not blush before the Wang house."

s0095.literal: The books he had kept in trust he soon handed over to him.
s0095.idiomatic: The books he had held in trust he soon entrusted to Huan.

s0096.literal: The province nominated him as Outstanding Talent; in the archery-and-writing examination he placed high.
s0096.idiomatic: The province nominated him as outstanding talent, and he placed high in the archery-and-writing examination.

s0097.literal: He began his career as chief secretary of Yangzhou and mobile aide on the staff of the Prince of Xuanhui of Xiangdong, but declined both appointments.
s0097.idiomatic: He was first named chief secretary of Yangzhou and mobile aide on the Prince of Xuanhui of Xiangdong's staff, but refused both posts.

s0098.literal: He was again appointed external military aide on the staff of the Prince of Xiangdong in the Campaign-West headquarters, entered court as Director of the Granary Bureau in the Masters of Writing, and was promoted to Gentleman in the Ceremonies Bureau.
s0098.idiomatic: He was again named external military aide on the campaign-west staff of the Prince of Xiangdong, entered court as director of the granary bureau, and rose to gentleman in the ceremonies bureau.

s0099.literal: At the time the Left Minister of the People Gentleman Shen Jiong was slandered by a flying petition and was about to fall into a capital offense; the affair touched the terrace offices, and men were fearful; Huan argued the case in court and at last secured his exoneration.
s0099.idiomatic: When the left minister of the people, Gentleman Shen Jiong, was attacked by an anonymous memorial and faced a capital charge, the affair implicated the terrace offices and everyone was afraid. Huan argued the case in open court and at last cleared him.

s0100.literal: He Jingrong, Metropolitan Governor of Danyang, because Huan was upright and firm, asked that he be appointed merit officer.
s0100.idiomatic: He Jingrong, metropolitan governor of Danyang, finding Huan upright and firm, asked to have him made merit officer.
